svg.title: A GPU falls to the level of the operator
svg.desc: Two horizontal bars compare generated output at P90 from two identical B200 serving stacks running the same model against the same interactivity target: about 200 tokens per second on one stack and about 300 on the other, roughly 50% more output from the same chip. The gap comes from software, settings, and request concurrency, all operator choices.

g.text: A GPU falls to the level of the operator
Buy by cost per acceptable token — grade the operator, not just the chip.
Two B200 serving stacks, same model, roughly 8,000 input and 1,000 output tokens.
P50 target of 100 output tokens per second per user; same assumed hourly bill for both.
generated tokens per second, measured at P90
“Same chip, same target interactivity, about 50% more output.”
The gap comes down to software, settings, and the number of requests running — all operator choices.
“Rating the operator is an essential building block for building a credible compute futures market.”
Source: Oliver Kennon (SemiAnalysis), “Not All GPU’s Are Deployed The Same”, AI Engineer NYC 2026, day 2.
